newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil industry sales rise 1.66 pct in October-CNI.
newsitem.headline: Brazil industry sales rise 1.66 pct in October-CNI.

text.p: Sales by Brazilian industry rose by a seasonally adjusted 1.66 percent in October compared with September, the private National Industry Confederation (CNI) said.
Sales in real terms rose 4.16 percent, CNI said.
October's sales were 13.03 percent higher than in October 1995.
Industry sales in the first 10 months of 1996 were up 4.93 percent from the same period last year, CNI said.
Brazilian industry was working at a seasonally adjusted average of 78.5 percent in October, up from 78.3 percent in September and 76.4 percent in October 1995, it said.
"These numbers dispel fears of overheating in industry that might have led to the introduction of measures to slow consumer demand," it said.
CNI attributed October's rising sales to falling interest rates and longer repayment terms for borrowers and said the figures represented continuing "modest" growth for industry.

It said the number of people employed in industry fell a seasonally adjusted 0.38 percent in October from September, was 4.72 percent lower than in October 1995, and was down 7.98 percent in the first 10 months of 1996.

The number of hours worked rose a seasonally adjusted 0.79 percent in October from September but was 3.65 percent lower than in October 1995 and was down 9.93 percent during the January-October period, it said.
